In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat al-Ahqaf

It is Meccan.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Ha Mim﴾. That is: Ha Mim, the matter has been decreed. Qatadah said: it is a name of the names of the Qur'an. Another said: it is an oath, and the answer to the oath is His saying: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾.
And His saying: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ has already been explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth﴾ means: except for reward and punishment. It is also said: except to establish the truth.

And His saying: ﴿and a specified term﴾ means: a limit at which it ends. This is an indication of the annihilation of the heavens and the earth after a known period.

And His saying: ﴿but those who disbelieve turn away from what they are warned of﴾ means: they turn away with the aversion of those who deny and reject.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 4:

His saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered those you invoke besides Allah?﴾ That is: the idols.

And His saying: ﴿Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens?﴾ That is: a share in the creation of the heavens, so that you would worship them for that. Its meaning is: they have no share, neither in the creation of the earth nor in the creation of the heaven, that is, no portion. So how can they be worshipped alongside Allah?!

And His saying: ﴿Bring me a Book from before this﴾ means: a Book from before the Qur'an that supports what you claim.

And His saying: ﴿Or a trace of knowledge﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: that is, a remnant of knowledge. It is said: "a she-camel with a trace (athara)," meaning a remnant of fat. It is also said: "or a trace of transmitted knowledge." Its meaning: if there is [with you] a book from the books of the earlier people, or transmitted knowledge [from them] which you see as supporting what you have said, then bring it, and show it to me if you are truthful. It is also said that "or a trace of knowledge" is the drawing of lines (khatt), and this is reported from Ibn 'Abbas. Mansur related from (Ibn Ibrahim) that a prophet among the prophets used to draw lines, and that this was the revelation to him. This has also been reported in a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report.

In some exegeses it is said: whoever draws lines has knowledge of what he has drawn. And from Ibn Ishaq, who said: the first to write with the pen was the Prophet Idris, peace be upon him.

And from (Mutarrif ibn al-Warraq), who said: His saying: ﴿or a trace of knowledge﴾ is the isnad (chain of transmission).

And His saying: ﴿if you are truthful﴾ means: truthful in what you say.

God's words: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, such as will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is: will never respond, ever.

And His words: ﴿while they are heedless of their calling﴾ That is: they do not hear their supplication even if they are called upon; and the intended meaning of the verse is the idols. That is: how can they worship the idols? Even if they called upon them, the idols would not respond to them and would not hear their speech.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them﴾, meaning: the idols will be enemies to them. ﴿And they will deny their worship﴾, meaning: they will say, "We did not call you to worship us."
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them as clear evidence, those who disbelieve say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is obvious magic."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 8:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it." Say, "If I have fabricated it, then you cannot avail me against Allah in the least."﴾ In the exegesis: Abu Jahl said to the Prophet, "O Muhammad, you are fabricating against Allah when you claim that this Qur'an is from His revelation and His speech, when it is only speech you utter from yourself."

And His saying: ﴿then you cannot avail me against Allah in the least﴾ means: if I have fabricated against Allah and He punishes me, you cannot avert His punishment from me.

And His saying: ﴿He is most knowing of what you pursue therein﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you﴾ means: Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful﴾, the meaning of which is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 9:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Say: I am not a novelty among the messengers, and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾. Its meaning: I was not the first messenger sent to the children of Adam. As for His words: ﴿and I do not know what will be done with me or with you﴾, al-Hasan al-Basri said: this refers to the world, but not to the Hereafter. Its meaning: in this world, and I do not know whether I will be left among you or killed. It is also said: I do not know whether I will be driven out as the prophets before me were driven out, or killed as the prophets before me were killed.

As for His words: ﴿or with you﴾, this is addressed to the disbelievers. Its meaning: I do not know whether you will be delayed in punishment or whether punishment will be hastened upon you. In some exegeses it is reported that when Allah the Most High revealed this verse, the Prophet and the believers were greatly grieved, i.e., they were saddened. So Allah the Most High revealed His words: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you a clear victory, that Allah may forgive you your previous and subsequent sins﴾. It was said to him: O Messenger of Allah, is this specifically for you, or is it for us as well? He said: "It is for me and for you, except that with which I have been favoured through prophethood." And the report is gharib (strange).

As for His words: ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am only a clear warner﴾, i.e., a warner who is manifestly a warner.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, and a witness from among the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it﴾. Ibn Sirin and a group said: it is Abdullah ibn Salam. This has also been narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah and others. According to this view, this verse is Medinan and part of the surah, because Abdullah ibn Salam embraced Islam in Medina by consensus.

In some reports: a group of Jews came to the Prophet, and the Messenger of Allah had placed Abdullah ibn Salam behind a screen. He said to them: "How is Ibn Salam among you?" They said: "He is our most knowledgeable and the son of our most knowledgeable, and our best and the son of our best."

The Prophet said: "Have you considered: if he were to embrace Islam, would you embrace it?" They said: "God forbid that he should embrace it." Then Abdullah ibn Salam came out and said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." They said: "He is our worst and the son of our worst, and our most ignorant and the son of our most ignorant," and they began to abuse him. This is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and a witness from among the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it﴾.

There is another view regarding the verse: that what is meant is a man from the Children of Israel in general. According to this view, the verse is Meccan, like the rest of the verses of the surah. There is a third view regarding the verse: that the witness from the Children of Israel is Musa, peace be upon him, who testified to the same as the Messenger testified concerning the oneness of Allah, the exalted, and that the worship of idols is false. This is the view of Masruq and others. In some exegetical works: that His saying ﴿and a witness from among the Children of Israel﴾ refers to Yamin ibn Yamin, who was one of the scholars of the Jews and embraced Islam at the hand of the Prophet. The first view is the well-known one.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿but you were arrogant﴾, meaning: he believed in what came with Muhammad, and you were too proud to believe in it after the truth had become manifest.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ is apparent in meaning. In the exegesis: there is an omission in the verse, and its implied sense is: "Say: Have you considered: if it is from Allah, and a witness from among the Children of Israel has testified to the like of it, and he believed while you were arrogant, have you not wronged yourselves and committed an ugly act that is not permissible?" Then He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾ as a new statement, meaning: the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 11:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who disbelieve say to those who believe﴾, to the end of the verse. It is related that a female slave called Zunayrah (Zunayrah) embraced Islam, and the idolaters of Quraysh said: "If there were any good in this religion, this slave-woman would not have preceded us to it." It is also said that she was a slave-woman of Umar ibn al-Khattab. In some exegetical works it is mentioned that this slave-woman went blind after she had embraced Islam, and the disbelievers said: "She was only afflicted with what she has been afflicted with because of her Islam." So Allah restored her sight to her.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: that Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Ghifar and Aslam believed in the Prophet, and they are tribes around Madinah. Banu Amir, Ghatafan, Asad and Ashja', who are the chiefs of the Arab tribes, said: "If there were any good in the religion, Muzaynah, Juhaynah, Aslam and Ghifar, the shepherds of the flocks, would not have preceded us to it." So Allah the Most High revealed this verse as a refutation of them.

As for His words: ﴿And when they are not guided by it﴾, that is: by the Qur'an and by what Muhammad (ﷺ) brought.

As for His words: ﴿they will say, "This is an ancient falsehood."﴾, that is: a narrative like the narratives of the earlier peoples, and it is a lie and a falsehood.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And before it was the Book of Musa﴾, meaning: a book before the Qur'an was the Book of Musa.

And His saying: ﴿an imam﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal).

And His saying: ﴿and a mercy﴾ is conjoined to it (ma'tuf 'alayhi).

And His saying: ﴿and this is a Book confirming﴾, meaning: confirming the Torah (al-Tawrat).

And His saying: ﴿in Arabic tongue﴾ is in the accusative also as a circumstantial state (hal). It is said that its meaning is: in the Arabic language (bi-lisan 'arabi).

And His saying: ﴿to warn those who have done wrong﴾, meaning: the Qur'an warns those who have done wrong. As for the one who reads it with the letter ta', meaning: "you (tundhir) warn, O Muhammad, those who have done wrong."

And His saying: ﴿and as good news for the doers of good﴾, with their faith and their righteous deeds.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 13:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾

And His saying: ﴿So no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ — we have already mentioned this as well.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those are the companions of Paradise, abiding therein as a reward for what they used to do.﴾ The verse is clear in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 15:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents. His mother carried him with difficulty and gave birth to him with difficulty.﴾ Al-kurh (الكره): it is al-ikrah (compulsion), and al-kurh (الكره) is the hardship in carrying when the load becomes heavy, and the hardship in giving birth at the time of labor. The meaning of al-kurh is close to this, i.e., with dislike on her part. In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: "She carried him with joy, and gave birth to him with joy." Al-Naqqash related from al-Farra' that al-kurh with a damma (الكُره) is joy, and al-kurh with a fatha (الكَره) is dislike; he related this.

And His saying: ﴿His carrying and his weaning is thirty months.﴾ Its meaning: the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, and the period of weaning is two years, and that totals thirty months. It is narrated that a woman brought forth a child six months after the marriage during the time of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him. ʿUmar intended to stone her, but ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "You have no authority over her," and he recited His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿His carrying and his weaning is thirty months.﴾ So ʿUmar said: "Had it not been for ʿAli, ʿUmar would have perished."

In some tafsirs: if the woman gave birth after six months, the period of weaning is twenty-four months, and if she gave birth after nine months, the period of weaning is [one] and twenty months. This contradicts the opinion of the jurists, for according to most jurists the period of weaning is two years in every case.

As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿until when he reaches his maturity﴾, we have already explained the meaning of ashudd (maturity).

And His saying: ﴿and reaches forty years﴾, we have also explained this, and it is the end of the period of full intellectual maturity.

And His saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, inspire me"﴾ means: grant me inspiration.

﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents, and to do righteousness of which You will approve, and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims.﴾ The meaning is apparent. The exegetes differed concerning who this verse was revealed about. Al-Kalbi, Muqatil and al-Dahhak said: it was revealed about Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: it is general concerning all believers. The meaning of the verse is guidance to thanking Allah and supplicating for one's parents.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 16:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Those are the ones from whom We accept the best of what they did﴾, meaning: the best of their deeds. And "the best of deeds" is everything that Allah, may He be exalted, is pleased with.

And His saying: ﴿and We overlook their evil deeds, among the companions of Paradise﴾, meaning: together with the companions of Paradise.

And His saying: ﴿a true promise which they were promised﴾, meaning: what they were promised of reward for righteous deeds. It is said that the first verse was revealed concerning Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who had embraced Islam, but his parents prevented him from Islam and pressed him hard to return from his religion, and we have explained this before. It is also said that it was revealed concerning his brother 'Umayr ibn Abi Waqqas. The meaning of the verse according to this is: the injunction to show kindness to them both, without agreeing with them in polytheism.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 17:

The words of God Most High: ﴿And he who says to his parents, "Uff to you both! Do you promise me that I will be brought forth, when generations have passed before me?"﴾ Some people of tafsir (exegesis) claimed that this verse was revealed concerning ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr, may Allah be pleased with them both, and that his parents were Abu Bakr and his mother Umm Ruman.

As for the words of God Most High: ﴿Uff to you both﴾, it expresses weariness and disgust. The two of them would say: "O Allah, guide him! O Allah, turn his heart [to faith]!" And he would say: "Do you threaten me that I will be (ub'ath), that is, do you threaten me with being resurrected?" This is the meaning of His words: ﴿Do you threaten me that I will be brought out?﴾

As for His words: ﴿And generations have already passed before me﴾, that is, the generations passed before me. [He was asking], "Where is ʿAbd Allah ibn Jadʿan? And so-and-so and so-and-so?"

As for His words: ﴿while they both call upon Allah for help﴾, that is, they both seek help from Allah.

As for His words: ﴿Woe to you! Believe, for the promise of Allah is true﴾, that is, woe to you (wayhak), believe, ﴿for the promise of Allah is true﴾.

As for His words: ﴿Then he says, "This is nothing but the myths of the former peoples."﴾ That is, the legends of the ancients. Many people of tafsir denied this statement, and it is narrated from ʿAʾishah that she used to deny that the verse refers to her brother. Likewise al-Zajjaj mentioned it in his book Maʿani [al-Quran] and others, and they argued for the weakness and invalidity of this view by the fact that God Most High said immediately after this verse:

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 18:

: ﴿Those are the ones against whom the word has been fulfilled, among nations that passed away before them of jinn and mankind.﴾ Meaning: the saying of punishment in the Fire has become due against them.

And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The word is not changed in My presence﴾. And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr embraced Islam and his Islam was good; he was one of the excellent Muslims. So the sound view is that the verse refers to someone other than him, namely the disbelieving, disobedient son toward his parents (ʿāqq li-wālidayhi) who died upon disbelief.

And His saying the Exalted: ﴿among nations﴾ means: together with nations.

And His saying: ﴿that passed away before them of jinn and mankind; indeed they were losers﴾ means: they were ruined.

His saying: ﴿And for each there are ranks according to what they did﴾ means: for each of the believers there are ranks according to what they did.

In the exegesis (tafsir) it is related that the ranks are of gold, silver, ruby, chrysolite, emerald, pearl and other jewels. In some reports it is said that God, exalted is He, will admit the believers into Paradise and will command them to divide it according to their deeds.

And His saying: ﴿That He may pay them in full their deeds, and they will not be wronged﴾ means: the evildoer's evil is not increased, and the good-doer's good is not diminished.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 20:

And the words of His, the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire: "You squandered your good things in your worldly life and enjoyed them."﴾ That is: you squandered your good things in the Hereafter through your disobediences in this world. It is also said: "The world preoccupied you, and you enjoyed it. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you were arrogant about in the earth, without right, [through] the desires, from obedience." It is also said: "You took your share in this world, so you have no share in the Hereafter."

And His words, ﴿and you enjoyed it﴾: that is, you took pleasure in it and benefited from it. In the well-known report: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) entered upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in his chamber, while he was lying on a [woven mat], part of him on the ground, and beneath his head was a cushion stuffed with palm fiber. In the room were some hides and a little tanning leaves. 'Umar wept, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "What makes you weep?" He said: "I remembered Kisra and Caesar and what they were in of blessings, and your state as I see it, while you are the Prophet of Allah, his chosen one and his best." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat up and said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things were hastened to them in their worldly life, and ours are deferred for us to the Hereafter."

It is also narrated that 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "How lovely is the pleasant life! If I wished, I could order young goats to be roasted for us, and order the finest wheat to be baked for us, and order raisins to be soaked for us until it becomes like the eye of the camel, so I eat of this once and drink of this once. But I heard Allah say to a people: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life﴾, and I fear that I may be one of them."

It is also narrated that he saw Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah with meat in his hand which he had bought. He said: "What is this?" He said: "I bought it for a dirham." He said: "Does each of you, whenever he gets up, buy meat for a dirham?" In another narration: "Whenever I desire, I buy. Did you not hear Allah say: ﴿You squandered your good things in your worldly life﴾? Or do you fear that you may be among them?"

And His words, ﴿Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾: that is, the humiliation (al-hawan), and it is thus in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud.

And His words, ﴿for what you were arrogant about in the earth without right﴾: that is, you sought exaltation and elevation [in the earth] without right. And for what you were defiant. And mention the brother of 'Ad, when he warned his people in al-Ahqaf, and warners had come before him and after him: "Worship none but Allah; I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day." They said: "Have you come to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten, if you are of the truthful." He said...

And [the commentary continues with]: "and the overpowering without right."

And His words, ﴿and for what you were defiant﴾: that is, you went out of obedience to Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 21:

And His the Exalted's saying: ﴿And mention the brother of ʿĀd﴾ — he is Hūd, peace be upon him, and he was their brother by lineage, not in religion.

And His saying: ﴿when he warned his people in al-Aḥqāf﴾. That is: his people, the ʿĀd. Al-Aḥqāf is the plural of ḥaqf (sand dune), which is a winding heap of sand. In a report: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed by a gazelle that was ḥāqif" — meaning its neck had bent. It is also said: al-Aḥqāf are elongated sand dunes resembling shops (dakākīn). And it was said: they are sand dunes overlooking the sea at al-Shiḥr in Yemen. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: a land between ʿUmān and Mahrah. And from Ibn Isḥāq: a land between ʿUmān and Ḥaḍramawt, where the dwellings of ʿĀd were. Abū al-Ṭufayl narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The worst well on earth is the well of the valley of Ḥaḍramawt called Barhūt, in which the spirits of the disbelievers are placed, and the best well on earth is the well of Zamzam." It is also said: they are mountains in al-Shām, but the more correct view is that they were in Yemen. As for the dwellings of Thamūd and the people of Lūṭ, they were between Madinah and al-Shām.

And His saying: ﴿And warners had already passed away before him and after him﴾. That is: warners had passed before Hūd and after him.

And His saying: ﴿Do not worship except Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous day﴾. That is: ʿaẓīm means kabīr (great).

﴿They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?"﴾ That is, to turn us away.

And His words: (Then bring us what you threaten us with). That is, the punishment.

And His words: ﴿If you are among the truthful﴾ meaning: if you are a prophet sent by God the Exalted.

"His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the knowledge is with Allah﴾ meaning: the time of your punishment is known to Allah, and I do not know it myself.

And His saying: ﴿And I convey to you that with which I have been sent, but I see you are a people acting ignorantly﴾. Its meaning: conveying the message is incumbent upon me, but sending down the punishment is not up to me; it rests only with Allah, Exalted is He."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 24:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿When they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys﴾. Al-'arid (cloud) here means the cloud. The poet said:

(When you look at the radiance of his face... it flashes like the lightning of the shining cloud.)

And another said:

(O you who sees a cloud that I have been watching all night... as if the lightning in its edges were torches.)

In the story: Allah the Exalted withheld the rain from them for three years, so they began to supplicate and ask Allah for rain. It is narrated that they sent a delegation to the Sacred House (al-Haram) asking for rain. They had a valley called al-Mughith, and their rain used to come from the direction of that valley. They saw a cloud coming from the side of that valley, and it was black, so they rejoiced and ﴿said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain."﴾ That is: a cloud that will send rain upon us. Hud, peace be upon him, who was sitting with them, said: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were hastening for: a wind wherein is a painful punishment.﴾

The Almighty's saying: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were hastening for﴾: they had said, "Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful." Ibn Ishaq mentioned that the first to see the punishment in the sky was a woman from among them, who said: "I see fires, and before them are men leading them."

In the story: the people of Hud said to Hud, "You threaten us with the wind, but which wind will overthrow us and destroy us?" It is related that Allah the Exalted commanded the angel who is in charge of the treasury of the wind to send the wind from the treasury. He said, "And how much shall I send it?" It was said to him, "In the measure of the nostril of an ox." He said, "Then it will overturn the earth with its inhabitants." It was said to him, "In the measure of the ring of a finger." So it was sent in this measure, and it began to lift the travelling litters (zu'n) between the sky and the earth, and it carried the herdsman with his sheep and camels, lifting them into the air, then hurling them down upon the mountains and crushing them. Thus it did to all of 'Ad until it destroyed them. In the exegesis: it carried men between the sky and the earth until they appeared like locusts. This punishment was imposed upon them for seven nights and eight days, consecutive (ḥusūman), as Allah the Exalted mentioned in another place.

In the story: Hud, peace be upon him, withdrew with those of his people who believed in him and drew a line for them, and the wind within that line was the gentlest and most pleasant of winds, and it wrought wonders for his people. It is related that when they saw the punishment and the wind was sent upon them, they entered their houses, which were of rock, and closed the doors. The wind broke open their doors, pulled them out of their houses, and drove the sand over them until it destroyed them beneath the sand, and the groaning of some of them could be heard beneath it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 25:

And His saying: ﴿Destroying everything by the command of its Lord﴾, meaning: by the permission of its Lord.

And His saying: ﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾. It is narrated that when God, exalted is He, destroyed them, He sent a great number of birds, until they snatched them up and cast them into the sea, so their dwellings became empty of all of them. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿So they became such that nothing could be seen except their dwellings﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Thus do We recompense the guilty people﴾, meaning: those who are possessors of crime (dhu al-ijram).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 26:

Regarding His the Exalted's words: ﴿And We had established them in that wherein We have not established you﴾ (wa-laqad makkannahum fima in makkannakum fih), there are three opinions. The first: "in that wherein We have not established you," meaning: We made their establishment and their bounties in the earth greater and more expansive.

The second opinion: "We established them in that wherein We established you," with "in" (in) being superfluous (silah).

The third opinion: there is an omission (hadhf) in the verse, and its estimated reading is: "And We had established you in that wherein We established them, and your obstinacy and insolence would have been greater," and this is the omitted part.

As for His words: ﴿And We made for them hearing﴾, meaning: hearings (asma'an).

As for His words: ﴿and sight and hearts﴾, meaning: eyes (a'yunan) with which they see, and hearts with which they know.

As for His words: ﴿But their hearing, nor their sight, nor their hearts availed them at all﴾, meaning: they did not repel from them, neither their hearing, nor their sight, nor their hearts, until the punishment descended upon them.

As for His words: ﴿anything, since they used to deny the signs of Allah﴾, meaning: they used to reject the signs of Allah.

As for His words: ﴿and there encompassed them﴾, meaning: there descended upon them.

As for His words: ﴿that which they used to mock﴾, meaning: its recompense.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 27:

Allah's words: ﴿And We had destroyed the towns around you, and We had varied the signs, that perhaps they would return.﴾ That is: the dwelling-places of ʿAd in Yemen, the dwelling-places of Thamud, and the cities of the people of Lut between Madinah and Syria. His words ﴿and We varied the signs﴾ mean: once We punished them, and once We bestowed favours upon them. It is also said: We frightened them once and fed them once.

His words ﴿that perhaps they would return﴾ mean: from the disbelief in which they were.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 28:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Why then did those whom they took as gods besides Allah not help them?⁠﴾ Its meaning: "Why did they not help them?" ﴿Those whom they took as gods besides Allah, as a means of approach⁠﴾, that is, the idols prevented Our punishment from them. As for His words ﴿as a means of approach⁠﴾, He only said that because they used to say: "Our worship of them brings us closer to Allah."

His words ﴿Rather, they strayed away from them⁠﴾, that is, they strayed away from worshipping the idols, and the idols never benefited them.

His words ﴿That was their lie and what they used to fabricate⁠﴾, that is, that was their falsehood and their fabrication.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 46, verse 29:

The Most High's words: ﴿And when We turned toward you a company of the jinn﴾, to the end of the verse. Its meaning: We turned their faces toward you.

As for the occasion of revelation of the verse: when the Prophet invited the disbelievers of Makkah to Islam and they refused to submit, he went out to al-Ta'if to call them to faith. When he returned to Makkah and was at Batn Nakhlah, a group of the nobles of the jinn of Nasibin passed by him while he was performing the dawn prayer. It is said that they saw him at Batn Nakhlah while he was heading to 'Ukaz. They differed about their number: some said they were seven men, and some said they were nine men. It is also said that Zawba'ah was among them. Their names are mentioned as Hasa, Masa, Yasa, Sha'ir, and Nasir, and Allah knows best. When they heard the recitation of the Prophet, they gathered to listen to it.

In the exegesis also: the jinn used to listen to the sky before the time of the Prophet; but when the time of the Prophet came, they were pelted with shooting stars. So they gathered and said: this is only because of a matter that has occurred on earth. So they traveled throughout the earth to the right and to the left until they found the Prophet at Batn Nakhlah praying and reciting the Qur'an, with the angels around him guarding him. So they understood that the matter that had occurred was for his sake.

As for His words: ﴿When they attended it, they said: Listen in silence﴾, meaning: some of them silenced others. It is related that some of them said to others: Sah, meaning: be quiet.

As for His words: ﴿When it was concluded﴾, its meaning: when he finished the recitation.

As for His words: ﴿they turned back to their people as warners﴾, meaning: as those who warn. It is also said: they turned back as callers to monotheism. It has been said that the jinn were from the jinn of Mosul, and that it is Nineveh, the town of Yunus ibn Matta. It is also said: from Harran. And it has been said other than that.

"The statement of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They said, "O our people, we have heard a Book revealed after Musa (Moses)."﴾ If it is asked: how is it that He mentioned "after Musa" and did not mention Isa (Jesus), when Isa is a prophet like Musa, peace be upon them both, and Allah also gave him the Injil, which is his Book? The answer to this: it is possible that they had not heard of the mention of Isa, and it is possible that they had heard of the mention of both Musa and Isa, but they mentioned Musa because he is earlier; and because most of the rulings in the Injil agree with what is in the Tawrah (Torah), except for a number of specific matters.

And His statement: ﴿confirming what is before it﴾ means: confirming what is before it of the Books.

And His statement: ﴿it guides to the truth and to a straight path﴾ means: upright (mustaqim)."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O our people, respond to the caller of Allah﴾, meaning: Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿And believe in him﴾, meaning: affirm him as true. ﴿He will forgive you of your sins and protect you from a painful punishment﴾, meaning: the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 32:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does not respond to the caller of Allah, he cannot cause failure [to Allah] on earth﴾, meaning: he cannot escape Allah or outrun Him.

And His saying: ﴿And he will not have protectors other than Him﴾, meaning: helpers [who would shield them] from the punishment.

And His saying: ﴿Those are in manifest error﴾, meaning: clear mistake. And in the reports: the delegation of the jinn went and warned their people, and then they returned to the Prophet (ﷺ) after a great many of them had embraced Islam. The Prophet (ﷺ) went out and recited the Qur'an to them and taught them the rulings. Regarding the account of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud accompanying him, there is much disagreement. It is reported that when he (ﷺ) wished to go to the jinn, he said: "Let there stand with me one of you who has in his heart no particle of mustard-seed of pride." So 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud stood up, and he (ﷺ) took him along with himself, drew a line for him, and said to him: "Beware that you leave this line." He (ﷺ) then went off to address the jinn. This gathering was at al-Hajun, which is a place at the upper part of Makkah. It is reported that when 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud heard their clamour and voices, he had suspicions about the Prophet (ﷺ), so he wanted to leave the line, but then he recalled the Prophet's (ﷺ) instruction and did not leave. He mentioned this to the Prophet (ﷺ) afterward, and he said: "Had you left, you would never have met me again." It is also reported that he saw some of them and saw traces of their fires.

There is much discussion on this, and varying narrations. In the narration of 'Alqamah from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, he said: "No one from among us was with him on the night of the jinn." And Allah knows best regarding that.

The scholars said: the verse is evidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to both the jinn and mankind.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 33:

And His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead?﴾ That is: He was not incapable of creating them. It was also said: He did not tire or become weary in creating them, unlike what the Jews said: that He grew weary from creating them and so rested on the Sabbath day.

And His saying: ﴿Able﴾ means: capable ﴿of giving life to the dead﴾.

And His saying: ﴿Yes, indeed He is over all things Powerful﴾ means: Capable.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the Day when those who disbelieved are exposed to the Fire (will be asked): "Is this not the truth?"﴾ Its meaning: it will be said to them, "Is this not the truth?"

And His saying: ﴿They will say, "Yes, by our Lord."﴾ That is: "Yes."

And His saying: ﴿He will say, "Taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾ That is: you used to disbelieve in Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 46, verse 35:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So be patient, as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾, meaning: be patient over what harm reaches you from the polytheists.

And His words: ﴿as the steadfast of the messengers were patient﴾. Most exegetes hold that they are four: Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them. Muqatil said: the steadfast (ulu al-'azm): Noah was patient over the harm of his people; Abraham was patient over the fire; Isaac was patient over being sacrificed; Jacob was patient over the loss of a son; Joseph was patient over prison; and Job was patient over affliction. It was also said: the steadfast are Noah, Hud, and Abraham. There is another opinion in the verse, and it is well known: that all the prophets are meant by the verse, and that "min" (from) is not partitive but explanatory. Whoever held this view said: there is no prophet who lacked resolve, firmness, judgment, or intellect; rather they all possessed these qualities. Among them are those who said: the steadfast of the messengers are those who were commanded to fight and to renounce the polytheists, so they fought and renounced them. In some of the Musnad collections, by way of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, it is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to her: "What have I to do with this world, O 'A'ishah? I was only commanded to be patient as the steadfast of the messengers were patient: they endured its hardships and they endured its pleasures," meaning: the hardships of this world and the pleasures of this world. "By Allah, I will do as they did, and I will strive until I attain the pleasure of my Lord." The report is gharib (rare). The opinion we mentioned last was reported by al-Kalbi and others, and according to these scholars, Adam is not among the steadfast, nor is Jonah, may the blessings of Allah be upon them both.

And His words: ﴿And do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them﴾. In the tafsir it is said that the Prophet was somewhat slow to see the punishment of the disbelievers; so Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse: ﴿And do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them﴾.

And His words: ﴿As if, on the day they see what they are promised, they had not remained but an hour of a day﴾. The day they are promised is the Day of Resurrection. And His words: ﴿A proclamation﴾, meaning: this is a proclamation, and it refers to the Qur'an. Abu Mijlaz Lahiq ibn Humayd read "balagh" in the form of a command.

And His words: ﴿Will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾, meaning: the disbelievers. The fasiq (defiantly disobedient) is one who departs from obedience to Allah, and that is the disbeliever. It is said that this is the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an. Qatadah said: none is destroyed before Allah except one who is already doomed; then he explained the doomed one, saying: he is a disbeliever who has turned his back on Islam, or a hypocrite who professes faith with his tongue while denying it in his heart.
